newsitem.title: MEXICO: POLL-Mexico's Penoles Q2 seen trending up.
newsitem.headline: POLL-Mexico's Penoles Q2 seen trending up.

text.p: Mexico's mining giant Industrias Penoles is seen posting upward-trending second quarter results compared with the same period last year, in part on beefed up own-mined metals output, analysts said.
A survey of four analysts polled by Reuters gave an average forecast of 0.71 peso earnings per share for the quarter against an unadjusted 0.61 peso per share in the second quarter of 1996.
Penoles, the world's top refined silver producer, posted earnings of 0.70 peso per share in the first quarter of 1997.

David Bodenberg, a consultant to Credit Lyonnais, said Penoles' drive for greater integration, pumping more of its own mine concentrates through smelters and refinery complexes, would shine through this quarter.
"A combination of strong zinc prices and higher proportions of own-mined zinc going through smelter complexes will help Penoles this quarter (against the second quarter of 1996)," Bodenberg said.
Other analysts agreed zinc prices would be the major positive factor in Penoles' balance sheet for the quarter.

Valores Finamex analyst Christopher Albi, predicting a more steady year-over-year balance sheet than other more bullish analysts, said zinc had risen 26 percent since the second quarter of 1996 according his calculations from LME prices.

Albi's take was that higher zinc prices would offset lower silver and gold prices. His calculations had second quarter silver prices off 10.5 percent year-over-year and gold down 12 percent in the same time period.

"The report is going to be steady. I see 21 percent operating margins (against 21 percent in the second quarter of 1996) and sales of $210 million in the period (compared with $211 million in the second quarter of 1996)," Albi said.
Silver accounts for around 35 percent of revenues, against around 13 percent for gold, around 17 percent for zinc and 15 percent for lead, according to Penoles data.
Some analysts, however, were predicting a slight decline in quarter-over-quarter earnings for Penoles.
"I see a slight dip in earnings for the quarter over the first quarter; prices are not favorable," said Hector Novoa, a mining analyst with Serfin brokerage in Mexico City.
